english: sometimes does; there are times when
use: Says something happens now and then; often with tama ni or tokidoki.
name: sometimes
formation: dictionary form or -nai form + koto ga aru

example.romaji: tama ni asagohan nuku koto aru yo
example.ja: たまに朝ご飯抜くことあるよ
example.english: I skip breakfast now and then.

examplePolite.romaji: tama ni asagohan o nuku koto ga arimasu
examplePolite.ja: たまに朝ご飯を抜くことがあります

notes: Don't mix with -ta koto ga aru, 'have done before'; only the verb form tells them apart.

use: The second thing happens without fail on each occasion.
name: every time
formation: dictionary form + tabi ni; noun + no tabi ni

example.romaji: kono uta kiku tabi ni naichau
example.ja: この歌聞くたびに泣いちゃう
example.english: I cry every time I hear this song.

examplePolite.romaji: kono uta o kiku tabi ni naite shimaimasu
examplePolite.ja: この歌を聞くたびに泣いてしまいます
examplePolite.english: I cry every time I hear this song.

notes: Close to -to itsumo; tabi ni stresses each single time.

use: From a past event until now, usually with something that has stayed true.
name: ever since

example.romaji: sotsugyou shite irai, zenzen atte nai ne
example.ja: 卒業して以来、全然会ってないね
example.english: We haven't seen each other at all since graduation.

examplePolite.romaji: sotsugyou shite irai, zenzen atte imasen ne
examplePolite.ja: 卒業して以来、全然会っていませんね
examplePolite.english: We haven't met at all since we graduated.

notes: Sounds a bit formal; casual talk often says -te kara zutto. 'sore irai' = ever since then.

english: just when I thought; no sooner ... than
use: Something unexpected follows right away, or the reality turns out different: 'I thought X, but'.
name: just when I thought

example.romaji: yatto hareta to omottara, mata ame da
example.ja: やっと晴れたと思ったら、また雨だ
example.english: Just when it finally cleared up, it's raining again.

examplePolite.romaji: yatto hareta to omottara, mata ame desu ne
examplePolite.ja: やっと晴れたと思ったら、また雨ですね
examplePolite.english: Just as it cleared up, it's raining again.

notes: It can also be a plain 'if you think': 'takai to omottara, kawanakute ii yo'. Context tells them apart.

english: in the middle of; right while
use: Usually for an interruption that came at a bad moment.
name: in the middle of
formation: -te iru form + saichuu ni; noun + no saichuu ni

example.romaji: kaigi no saichuu ni onaka ga natchatta
example.ja: 会議の最中にお腹が鳴っちゃった
example.english: My stomach growled right in the middle of the meeting.

examplePolite.romaji: kaigi no saichuu ni onaka ga natte shimaimashita
examplePolite.ja: 会議の最中にお腹が鳴ってしまいました
examplePolite.english: My stomach rumbled in the middle of the meeting.

notes: Stronger than -te iru aida (while). 'ima saichuu' = I'm right in the middle of it.

english: the moment that; as soon as
use: The second thing happens instantly and usually unexpectedly.
name: the moment

example.ja: 座った途端に寝ちゃった
example.english: He fell asleep the second he sat down.

examplePolite.ja: 座った途端に寝てしまいました
examplePolite.english: He fell asleep the moment he sat down.

notes: Not for your own plans: 'as soon as I get home, I'll call' is -tara sugu.

english: is; there is, we have (very polite)
use: Shop and hotel staff use it in place of desu and arimasu; you mostly hear it rather than say it.
name: very polite is / has
formation: noun + de gozaimasu (= desu); noun + ga gozaimasu (= arimasu)

example.romaji: kochira ga atarashii moderu de gozaimasu
example.ja: こちらが新しいモデルでございます

notes: The dictionary form gozaru is archaic. You do say it in set phrases: arigatou gozaimasu, ohayou gozaimasu, omedetou gozaimasu.

use: The standard polite request to strangers, staff and people at work; -te itadakemasen ka is softer still.
name: could you kindly

example.ja: すみません、写真撮っていただけますか
example.english: Excuse me, could you take our photo?

notes: One step politer than -te moraemasu ka. Literally 'can I receive the favour of you doing'.

english: kindly do (for me), said of someone above you
use: The respectful -te kureru: a teacher, boss or customer does something for you.
name: kindly do (respectful)

example.romaji: sensei ga eki made okutte kudasatta n da
example.ja: 先生が駅まで送ってくださったんだ
example.english: My teacher kindly took me to the station.

examplePolite.romaji: sensei ga eki made okutte kudasaimashita
examplePolite.ja: 先生が駅まで送ってくださいました
examplePolite.english: My teacher was kind enough to take me to the station.

notes: Common in thanks: 'kite kudasatte arigatou gozaimasu' (thank you for coming). -te kudasai is its request form; never use it for your own actions.

use: Announces your own action very politely, as if asking permission; everywhere in business, shops and speeches.
name: humbly do
formation: causative -te form + itadaku (yasumasete, ikasete, shitsurei sasete)

example.romaji: kyou wa kore de shitsurei sasete itadakimasu
example.ja: 今日はこれで失礼させていただきます
example.english: If you'll excuse me, I'll be leaving now.

notes: Overused in business talk, so it can sound stiff. With friends, just say -sasete or -sasete morau.

use: Tucks a yes/no question into a sentence, usually before wakaranai, kiku or shiraberu.
name: whether or not
formation: plain form + ka dou ka (noun or na-adjective drops da)

example.romaji: kare ga kuru ka dou ka wakannai
example.ja: 彼が来るかどうかわかんない
example.english: I don't know whether he's coming.

examplePolite.romaji: kare ga kuru ka dou ka wakarimasen
examplePolite.ja: 彼が来るかどうかわかりません
examplePolite.english: I don't know if he's coming or not.

notes: With a question word, use plain ka: 'itsu kuru ka wakaranai'.

english: just as; the way (said, planned, shown)
use: Something matches what was said or shown; iu toori, 'just as you say', is the most common.
name: just as
formation: dictionary or -ta form + toori; noun + no toori; noun + doori

example.romaji: iwareta toori ni yatta kedo, dame datta
example.ja: 言われたとおりにやったけど、ダメだった
example.english: I did exactly what I was told, but it didn't work.

examplePolite.romaji: iwareta toori ni yarimashita ga, dame deshita
examplePolite.ja: 言われたとおりにやりましたが、ダメでした
examplePolite.english: I did it exactly as instructed, but it didn't work.

notes: 'sono toori' = exactly, that's right. 'yotei doori' = as planned.

english: speaking of; when you think of
use: Picks up a word just said to shift topic, or names the classic example: 'kyouto to ieba otera'.
name: speaking of
formation: noun or plain form + to ieba

example.romaji: natsu to ieba, yappari suika da yo ne
example.ja: 夏といえば、やっぱりスイカだよね
example.english: When you think summer, it's got to be watermelon.

examplePolite.romaji: natsu to ieba, yappari suika desu yo ne
examplePolite.ja: 夏といえば、やっぱりスイカですよね
examplePolite.english: Speaking of summer, watermelon is the classic, isn't it?

notes: Sou ieba is the stand-alone 'that reminds me'. Casual: 'X tte ieba'.

english: it means that; I hear that
use: Sums up or draws a conclusion ('so that means...'), or passes on news you heard.
name: that means
formation: plain form + to iu koto da

example.romaji: jaa, kyanseru to iu koto da ne
example.ja: じゃあ、キャンセルということだね

examplePolite.romaji: jaa, kyanseru to iu koto desu ne
examplePolite.ja: じゃあ、キャンセルということですね

notes: Casual speech says tte koto: 'kyanseru tte koto?'. On the news, '... to iu koto desu' means 'reportedly'.

use: Names the source of what you heard; the sentence usually ends in -sou da, rashii or tte.
name: according to

example.romaji: tenki yohou ni yoru to, ashita wa yuki rashii yo
example.ja: 天気予報によると、明日は雪らしいよ
example.english: According to the forecast, it's going to snow tomorrow.

examplePolite.romaji: tenki yohou ni yoru to, ashita wa yuki da sou desu
examplePolite.ja: 天気予報によると、明日は雪だそうです
examplePolite.english: According to the weather forecast, it'll snow tomorrow.

notes: Not the same as -ni yoru, 'it depends on'. -ni yoreba means the same and sounds more formal.
